# A shared original plane: a precise surviving mode and its obstruction

The one-group homothetic escape does not automatically control another
cap group. This note records an actual sufficient condition that
retains one shared original cap exactly, gives a concrete two-group
example, and identifies an exact obstruction from a full trace.
The example is not an inclusion-minimal multigroup cover: its first
concurrent group already covers the whole ambient space.

## 1. Shared-plane compatibility of the meeting mode

Let a compatible homothetic simplex family have a freely variable
selected fiber, normalized to K with volume V. Assume its one-group
quantity

    Theta=d(S-1)^2+1-N_2

is positive. This holds in particular for a smallest-radius fiber
when another positive fiber exists, as proved in
global-cap-baseline-curvature-and-one-fiber-canonical-escape.md.
Here the starting family must already have the required open
compatibility neighborhood. A preliminary radial change cannot
be assumed to preserve the budgets of additional groups.

Let group A be its canonical group with fixed normals l_i and
common threshold vector tau. Suppose a second group B shares
precisely the original cap e, and leave EVERY cap of B fixed.
The permitted common-translation velocities satisfy

    sum_i v_i=0, v_e=0.                                   (1)

Use tau(t)=t v exactly, not just to first order. Then the shared
cap l_e>=0 never moves. The physical acceleration changes a fiber,
not any cap equation, so it cannot break that identity. Group A
continues to cover all space because sum tau_i=0; group B retains
all its original coefficients, positive circuit, and projected
coverage.

This is the exact specialization of the shared-original equations:
the meeting motion y(t) satisfies l_e(y(t))=0, and the shared
normal and its full affine base coefficients are unchanged.
No duplicated occurrence receives an independent threshold.

For d>=2, the space in (1) has dimension d-1. The optimized physical
matrix B(v) from the one-group theorem still gives

    Q(v)=V m(d-1)Theta ||v||^2/d>0                         (2)

for every nonzero v in that space. Thus shared-plane compatibility
alone does not eliminate the positive one-group mode.

## 2. The actual additional budgets

Keep all other source fibers fixed. For each private cap J of group B,
its entire mass increment is exactly its increment on the one
physically varied fiber. There are two useful sufficient cases:

* If J is strictly empty on that fiber, its budget stays exactly
  unchanged for every sufficiently small physical perturbation.
* If J is a proper cut and its first physical derivative along B(v)
  is strictly negative, its budget strictly decreases for small
  positive time, regardless of the finite second acceleration
  used to pay the canonical A caps.

The latter derivative is explicit. Let V_B(x) be the affine
velocity field of the labeled simplex motion B(v), and let
J={u.x>=b}. At the canonical critical velocity, tr B(v)=0, so

    E_J(v)= integral_(K intersect boundary J)
                   u.V_B(x) dH^(d-1)(x)/|u|.              (3)

For a general physical velocity a further term
(tr B)|K intersect J| appears. Formula (3) follows by pulling
the fixed cap through the affine body map, differentiating its
determinant and its scalar threshold. Properness is sufficient
for this first derivative.

Consequently a nonzero v satisfying (1), and E_J(v)<0 for every
additional proper private cap while all remaining private caps
are strictly empty, supplies a genuine two-group nonincrease path.
The A caps all decrease to second order and total mass increases
to second order by (2) and its physical acceleration. The additional
proper caps decrease to first order; the empty ones stay fixed.
This is a concrete finite system of strict linear inequalities
in v together with (1).

If an additional proper cap has E_J(v)=0, its second derivative
and its interaction with the physical acceleration must be
checked. The one-group Hessian alone supplies no sign for it.

## 3. A strict full trace blocks this one-fiber transfer

There is a simple exact obstruction. Suppose a fixed private cap
of B contains the entire selected fiber with a strict margin.
The same is true for every nearby physical perturbation. With
all other fibers and that cap fixed,

    increment of its global cap mass
       = increment of the selected fiber's volume
       = increment of the total mixed mass.               (4)

Thus any strict total mass gain violates this cap's nonincrease
constraint, even though its first derivative on a critical
trace-zero mode is zero. Equation (4) concerns the full nonlinear
path and cannot be repaired merely by satisfying first-order
shared-plane equations.

This obstruction does not rule out moving that private cap,
moving another source fiber, or using other group parameters.
It shows exactly why a zero first derivative of an additional
cap cannot be silently discarded.

## 4. Two exact planar calibrations with one shared original

Take two identical fibers at integer bases 0,1, both

    K=conv{(-1/3,-1/3),(2/3,-1/3),(-1/3,2/3)}.

Their actual convex body is [0,1] times K. These are exposed bases,
so either fiber is independently perturbable. Total mass is one.
Use the cylindrical group

    A:  -x-y>=0, x>=0, y>=0.

Each A cap has global mass 4/9. Share x>=0 with the group

    B:  x>=0, -y+z-1>=0, -x+y+2z-2>=0.                   (5)

Its normals have positive dependence (1,1,1); its projected
margin is z-1. At base zero its two private caps are strictly
empty on K, with maximum margins -2/3 and -1. At base one the
group covers the entire continuous fiber. Their global budgets
are respectively 5/18 and 1/4.

Choose the selected fiber at base zero. In A's barycentric order
(l0,l1,l2)=(-x-y,x,y), use

    v=(1,0,-1).

The shared cap has v1=0. Here S=N_2=2, Theta=1, and the maximizing
physical matrix is

    B(v) = [ 5 -1  2
            -3  0  3
            -2  1 -5 ].

Its column sums and trace vanish, and its row sums are 6v.
The normalized Hessian is Q/V=3; since V=1/2, Q=3/2.
The one-group physical acceleration therefore supplies an exact
nearby path with larger mass and all three A budgets strictly
smaller. Both private B budgets stay exactly 5/18 and 1/4.
The shared original remains x>=0 throughout and is counted once.

For the opposite calibration replace only group B by

    B_full: x>=0, -y+1-z>=0, -x+y+4z-4>=0.               (6)

It has the same continuous circuit and projected margin z-1,
and the same shared cap. At base zero its first private cap is
strictly full on K, with minimum margin 1/3. Its second private
cap is strictly empty. Thus, with (6) fixed, equation (4) blocks
EVERY volume-increasing one-fiber path at base zero, including
the mode just displayed.

Both calibrations use actual full-dimensional convex sources
and oblique original halfspaces. They distinguish exact group
compatibility from additional cap-budget compatibility.
The first group alone already covers the source, so neither
example is an inclusion-minimal five-cap cover. The budgets
also exceed the n=1,d=2 OC target 2/9. No inference about
minimal high-cardinality or below-target covers follows.

The exact verifier is
verify_shared_original_fixed_plane_mode_transfer.py.
